instruction_text:
CHECKPOINT TURN.
Every fact you need may sit behind a marker of the form `[MASKED <ref>]`, where `<ref>` is exactly `doc-<name>@r<revision>` (for example `[MASKED doc-constants@r1]`).
Two protocols, kept separate:
(1) RETRIEVAL. When markers are present you MUST, in a single round, issue one fetch call for EVERY ref that appears as a `[MASKED <ref>]` marker, then answer from the returned bodies. Answering before fetching every marker is a protocol violation and is recorded as `retrieval_omitted`. Worked example (two calls in one round): fetch(ref="doc-config@r1") and fetch(ref="doc-constants@r1").
(2) ANSWERING. While working a turn you MAY reply with a TOOL CALL instead of an `ANSWER:` line. A tool call is NOT an answer and must NOT carry the `ANSWER:` prefix. Use the structured shape the tool schema expects, e.g. {"name":"fetch","arguments":{"ref":"doc-config@r1"}}. One round may contain several such calls, e.g. three: {"name":"fetch","arguments":{"ref":"doc-config@r1"}}, {"name":"fetch","arguments":{"ref":"doc-constants@r1"}}, {"name":"fetch","arguments":{"ref":"doc-errors@r1"}}. After the tool results come back, reply with the `ANSWER:` line.
`ANSWER: CALL <name>(...)` is reserved for an answer whose CONTENT is a call; it is never used for retrieval.
Emit exactly one line and nothing else, in this contract (the answer line comes after retrieval, never wrapped around a fetch):
  ANSWER: NUM <integer>
  ANSWER: CALL <callee>(<kw>=<value>, <kw>=<value>, ...)
  ANSWER: NONE
  ANSWER: TEXT <one line of prose>
For CALL, put the keyword arguments in alphabetical order and give each value as the source text shows it. Anything written after that line is not read.
violation_guard: row['protocol_violation'] = 'answer_wrapped_tool_call' when an ANSWER: payload begins with 'CALL fetch('; counted separately from a genuine wrong answer. Helper run_longrun.protocol_violation() and checkpoint_answer_fields() expose the same field.
